updates.statement: Per-epoch GPU work drives the score. Current state: E090 (2@16 + 1.25@24 at bs 1536, then 1.25@28 + 2.75@32 at bs 1024, Fable tail, pinned staging) runs at ~4.46 s but is feasible only by luck. Its distinct scored samples are 0.7531 and 0.7517, and its distinct off-seed samples are 0.7531 and 0.7515, a mean of ~0.7524, below 0.753. The only robustly feasible config is the E084/E085/E095 family (bs 1024 at 32 px): distinct pool 0.7549 at ~4.70 s. Every route that shrinks the 32 px phase costs ~0.05-0.065 pp per 1% of time: the trim (E089), the equal-step 28 px substitution (E090) and the older whole-epoch shift (E025). So further time must come from math-neutral levers or be paid for with new accuracy. Cost structure: the 32 px phase is ~71% of time and energy-bound; 16 px is low-occupancy. Remaining time levers: (a) cudnn.benchmark_limit=0 in the untimed build (math-equivalent, untested; H2.14); (b) depth cuts, which remove whole kernels and so escape tile quantization (profile first). Closed: CUDA graphs/launch (E052), Inductor pointwise tuning (E066), hand-fused BN backward, cuDNN determinism (E036), prepare (E060, E086), whitening-bias freeze (the detach is already in the code; the earlier freeze in E093 cost -0.44 pp), width cuts (E080), 32 px trims and the 28 px substitution (E089, E090).
updates.reason: The review showed the statement was stale: wrong tip, a provenance question that is already settled, and levers ranked that are already banked or already present in the code. Rewritten around the E090 (lucky) vs E095 (robust) pair and the measured cost of shrinking the 32 px phase.

updates.statement: Step-indexed schedule reshuffles and trims are no longer a usable lever at the current margin. Low-res reshuffles are exhausted: E070/E071 vs E072/E073 are equivalent at equal time. The 32 px phase is binding: a 0.25-epoch trim (E088/E089) cost ~0.33 pp against its base pool for ~-5% time (~0.065 pp per 1%).
updates.reason: Its last open child H2.10.5 is refuted by E089 (pool 0.7522 vs E084 pool 0.7555), and the low-res plateau was already established. Nothing untested remains under this mechanism.
E088~ E089-: the pooled loss of ~0.33 pp is beyond the <=0.2 pp bar and above the 0.3 pp 'binding' threshold. The status had been left open by mistake.

updates.statement: Per-phase batch size. Large early batches hurt (E043: bs 2048 at 16/24 px, -0.49 pp). Smaller batches in the 32 px phase help: bs 1024 there gave +0.12-0.18 pp scored and +0.10-0.11 pp off-seed over three distinct runs (E084/E085/E095), at +2.5% time (~0.05-0.07 pp per 1%). E095 pinned the EMA window to 8 steps and kept the gain, so the effect comes through update count (or Muon path length, see the H10 path-length child), not the longer averaging window. The exchange rate is about equal to the 32 px trim rate, so it buys back what a trim costs but does not fund a net cut. Untested: going further (bs 768 at 32 px).
updates.reason: H2.11.3 and H2.11.4 are both supported by replicated results (E084+, E085+, E095+); rolled up.

E084 0.7560 and E085 0.7550 (pool 0.7555, +0.18 pp vs the tip pool), off-seed +0.11 pp, time +2.5%. The prediction's off-seed +0.15 bar was not fully met, but the scored pool cleared +0.1 pp, and E095 replicated the result. The status had been left open by mistake.

E095+: with the window pinned to 8 steps, off-seed was 0.75405 (= E084's 0.7541) and scored 0.7537. That is the same size as E084's gain, so the window is not the mechanism. This rests on a single run within ~1 SE of E084, hence moderate confidence.

updates.statement: Compile, graph and transfer configuration is a FLOP-neutral time lever. Banked so far: static per-resolution graphs (-2.0%, E053), max(dim).values instead of AdaptiveMaxPool2d (-2.9%, E056; amax produces NaNs under torch 2.4 Inductor, E055), and a pinned staging buffer allocated in build (-0.5%, E086/E087, bit-identical). Changes that are math-equivalent but not bit-equivalent are fine. The one untested candidate is cuDNN's algorithm search width (cudnn.benchmark_limit, default 10; 0 = try all), which runs in the untimed build.
updates.reason: Added E086 to the banked list. Search found an untried math-neutral knob (benchmark_limit).
E086+ E087+: trial-1 prepare fell from 0.098 to 0.034 s, the run was bit-identical, and mean time fell 0.5%. The status was 'retired' even though the result supports it.

The premise was already in the tip: E093's precondition found the whiten_bias_grad=False detach graph already present, so this lever is already banked. The earlier freeze (H2.15.2) is refuted by E093. The opposite direction (freeze later, or never) is moved under the new late-full-res Lvl1 as an accuracy test.
Moot: the detach at the 20% point is already in the tip code (E093 precondition).
E093-: off-seed -0.44 pp and scored 0.7475, for -0.7% time. That is about 3 SE, one of only two recent off-seed effects that are clearly real.

updates.statement: An intermediate 28 px stage that replaces part of the 32 px phase while keeping the step count is no cheaper in accuracy than trimming 32 px epochs. E090 lost ~0.25 pp against its base family (E084/E085/E095, distinct pool 0.7549) for ~-5.1% time. With E094 included, its distinct pool (~0.7524) equals the trim arm's (0.7522). Keeping the step count bought nothing: exposure to the 32 px resolution itself binds.
updates.reason: E090~ E094-: the claimed +0.09 pp edge over the trim came from counting the bit-identical E091 rerun. Distinct samples put the loss at ~0.25 pp, about twice the <=0.12 pp prediction, on two scored and two off-seed samples.
E090~ E091(bit-identical, not counted) E094-: accuracy loss ~0.25 pp vs the predicted <=0.12, i.e. ~0.05 pp per 1%, the same rate as the trim. The time part (-2.2% vs E086, -5% vs its base) held.

updates.statement: Accuracy noise sets the usable margin, and decisions near the gate select for luck. The per-run sd of the 3-seed mean is ~0.1-0.15 pp, and per-seed sd is 0.22-0.38 pp. Rules: bit-identical reruns count once. A keep requires >=2 non-bit-identical scored samples with mean >=0.7535. Family membership is decided by code diffs. The loop broke this rule again with E090: it was kept on one effective sample at 0.7531, and its first distinct rerun gave 0.7517 (distinct mean ~0.7524). E090 is therefore feasible-by-luck, not banked. E095 (distinct pool 0.7549 at ~4.70 s) is the robust fallback. Off-seed verdicts use seeds 3-10 (SE ~0.1-0.13 pp paired, from per-seed sd/sqrt(8)). Only E083 (-0.29) and E093 (-0.44) clear ~2 SE. Extend to seeds 3-26 to halve the SE before further near-zero verdicts. The official gate is a 40-seed mean at 0.75, which E090 likely clears (~0.7525); the local 0.753 gate is the binding one.
updates.reason: Review: the E090 keep repeated the H4.2 failure mode. Folded in E094 and the stricter keep rule.

updates.statement: Run-to-run noise (~0.1-0.15 pp sd on a 3-seed mean), not cross-seed std, is the decision-relevant noise floor. Picking whichever near-threshold variant first clears 0.753 selects for luck. This happened with E026 (~0.1 pp lucky), E046 (~0.2 pp), E068 (tail, one high draw) and E090 (one effective sample at 0.7531; distinct mean ~0.7524). Every comparison must use pooled distinct samples.
updates.reason: E090/E094 is a fourth instance of the pattern.

updates.statement: Provenance check, untimed and free. Settled: E070 contains the Fable tail, and E067 is bit-identical to E062. Still to do: (1) git-diff 772c536 (E077), bc2ffe6 (E078), 3d7548e (E079), 2940f3c (E081), f610c4c (E083) and 3e30852 (E084) against their stated base; (2) resolve E092/E093, whose ideas name E086 code as the base but whose outcomes say 'on E090'. Then recompute their off-seed deltas against the correct baseline: E090 is ~0.7523, not 0.7530. That would shrink E092's -0.18 pp to ~-0.11 pp, about 1 SE. Any mismatch removes the run from its A/B.
updates.reason: The review found a new provenance and baseline inconsistency for E092/E093.

E094~: the sd of ~0.09 pp comes from only two distinct off-seed values (0.7531, 0.7515), so the CI covers more than an order of magnitude. It is consistent with per-seed sd/sqrt(8) (~0.08-0.13). Clustering by checksum held, but that is just determinism, not calibration.

E094: identical off-seed results go with identical weight checksums, and differing results go with differing checksums. This supports the claim that rerun differences come from training divergence via cuDNN pick sets, with no eval-only mode observed.
E094+: an identical checksum always gave identical accuracy, and no seed had identical weights with different accuracy. The status had been left open.

updates.statement: Part of the run-to-run variance might be a per-run offset shared by all trials, from the cuDNN pick set cached once per process. Current evidence does not require it: per-seed sd (0.22-0.38 pp)/sqrt(n) already accounts for the observed ~0.1-0.15 pp run sd. E094 shows only that the same pick set gives the same result (determinism), not that some pick sets are systematically worse. It is worth checking only as a free by-product of the benchmark_limit test, which changes the pick sets.
updates.reason: Review: no evidence of an offset. Downgraded, and attached to the new benchmark_limit test.
No data yet. Run it as a side log of the benchmark_limit=0 experiment rather than as standalone runs.

updates.statement: Zero-time-cost accuracy levers on the current architecture and schedule. Scalar knobs are exhausted: Muon floor, warmup in both directions, head lr 0.4x, head wd, MaxSup, LS 0.2, the bias freeze earlier (E093) and at 20% (E061), lookahead removal (E092), and EMA window/LAWA with BN buffers copied from the net (E081, E083). The one remaining candidate with external support is end-of-run averaging that keeps the BN buffers consistent with the averaged weights (H6.5.4; search 2411.18704: BN, not the parameters, breaks long-window EMA). Phase-local Muon lr is under H10, and filter Muon lr under H7. Retire H6 if H6.5.4 fails.
updates.reason: Review: every candidate listed under H6 has now been run without a gain (E092 refuted lookahead removal). It is kept open narrowly only because the search raised the prior for the BN-buffer mechanism.

updates.statement: End-of-run schedule under Muon. The tail (floor-hold at ~96% of steps, lookahead stop, final 8-step EMA at 0.3 lerp every 4, eval on EMA weights with BN buffers from the net) costs no time and is kept. Its mean gain was never shown, though: the evidence is E068 (one high draw) and E069, and no tail vs no-tail off-seed A/B was ever run. Longer windows lost off-seed (E081 -0.09, ~1 SE; E083 LAWA -0.29, ~2 SE). Two explanations compete: (a) averaging higher-LR pre-floor iterates hurts; (b) the averaged weights mismatch the BN buffers copied from the net. External work (2411.18704) directly supports (b). Only H6.5.4 separates them.
updates.reason: Review: stop citing the tail as an accuracy source. Search raised the prior for mechanism (b).

This was gated on a tail vs no-tail off-seed A/B that was never run. E079's -0.18 pp off-seed is ~1.4 SE, a single run, and was compared against the wrong-family baseline question. It does not establish the component split.

updates.statement: Discriminating test between the two mechanisms, with a possible accuracy gain at zero time cost. On the E090 config, use E081's 20-step final EMA (0.3 lerp every 4 steps), but also lerp the BN running_mean/var buffers with the same weights (AveragedModel use_buffers=True style) instead of copying them from the final net. Do this in the existing foreach_lerp, with buffers allocated in build and nothing recompiling. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 against E090 on the same seeds. Prediction (BN mismatch, search 2411.18704): the buffer-averaged 20-step EMA is >= E090 +0.05 pp, against E081's -0.09 with copied buffers. If it is <= E090 -0.05 pp, the iterate-LR explanation holds, and end-of-run averaging and H6 close.
updates.reason: Search (2411.18704) directly supports the BN-mismatch mechanism, so the prior rises. Reframed so the test can also pay off as a zero-time accuracy source on the current tip.
Low prior (0.08), and the relevant literature points the other way (TSLA). Uniform LS changes and MaxSup were null or negative. Review: no positive expected value.
Its parent H6.7 is retired.

E092-: removing lookahead cost -0.18 pp off-seed (about -0.11 against E090's own baseline, see H4.2.4) and scored 0.7499, for only -0.4% time. Even after re-baselining, the trade is worse than any exchange rate on the table.
E092-: the off-seed loss is >=0.1 pp under either baseline and the scored loss is ~-0.25 pp, at a -0.4% time gain.

updates.statement: Optimizer quality per update was the binding constraint on CIFAR-100 at ~7-8 epochs, and Muon was the lever: +1.14 pp at equal epochs (E019), a flatter epoch slope (E020) and large-batch tolerance (E022, E038). Head on Muon and head lr 0.5x are each worth ~+0.1-0.2 pp on weak evidence. Closed: momentum (flat 0.5-0.6), NS count, cheaper orthogonalizers, head lr/wd. The Muon lr optimum (flat at 0.20-0.24) was measured on the bs-1024, head-on-SGD E026 base. Whether it transfers to the mixed-batch E090 tip (bs 1536 low-res, bs 1024 at 28/32 px) is untested (H7.1.3). The phase-local version is under H10.
updates.reason: Refreshed for the current mixed-batch tip, per the review.
Still supported on its own base (E027, E030, E034), but that base no longer exists. Confidence lowered a little because the transfer to the mixed-batch tip is untested.

updates.statement: On the E090 config (bs 1536 at 16/24 px, bs 1024 at 28/32 px, head Muon lr 0.5x), change only the conv-filter Muon lr from 0.24 to 0.28 in every phase. The head stays at 0.5x and scales along, as a 0-d tensor, so nothing recompiles. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 against E090 on the same seeds, plus two distinct scored samples. Prediction: off-seed mean >= E090 +0.1 pp. If it is within ±0.05 pp, run 0.20 off-seed only; if both are flat, Muon lr is closed. Lower priority than the 32 px-only lr test under H10, which isolates the path-length mechanism.
updates.reason: Rebased onto the mixed-batch tip and the extended off-seed instrument. Ranked below the more targeted phase-local test that search suggested.

updates.statement: On the Muon tip, at fixed epochs and resolution split, adding optimizer updates in the 32 px phase raises accuracy at roughly the rate of the 32 px trim: bs 1024 at 32 px gave +0.1-0.18 pp for +2.5% time (E084/E085/E095). Removing steps everywhere costs accuracy (E038 -0.12 pp; E022 -0.25 pp). The corollary 'substitutions that keep the step count beat trims' failed: E090 kept every step and lost as much as the trim (H2.17). So the step count does not bind on its own; what binds is 32 px exposure, steps in that phase, or both. Open questions: (a) whether added low-res steps help as much (H10.1, against the competing late-full-res Lvl1); (b) whether the gain is update count or Muon path length (lr × steps), since Muon's update size is set by the lr.
updates.reason: Review: E090 refutes the H10 corollary. Search added the path-length alternative. Confidence lowered.

No new evidence. E090 slightly weakens placement-independence (an equal step count with less 32 px exposure lost accuracy), and the competing late-full-res Lvl1 now gives the opposite prediction for H10.1.1.

updates.statement: On the E090 config, run the 16 and 24 px phases at bs 1024 too, making the whole run bs 1024. The 28/32 px phases and the tail are unchanged. This adds ~50 low-res steps. LR is indexed by samples; the SGD groups are scaled per phase by the kilostep rule; Muon lr/momentum are unchanged; the bs-1024 16/24 px static shapes are warmed up in build. Pre-registered time: +1.5-2.5%. Prediction (placement-independent): off-seed seeds 3-26 gain of +0.05 to +0.15 pp. If the gain is <=+0.03 pp, low-res steps are not worth it, and the late-full-res Lvl1 replaces H10's placement claim. If it is >=+0.2 pp, early steps are worth more. Pass bar for keeping it: >0.065 pp per 1% of time, with two distinct scored samples.
updates.reason: Rebased onto the current tip, which already runs bs 1024 at 28/32 px. Uses the extended off-seed instrument and a pre-registered exchange-rate bar.

new.statement: Accuracy at the tip is bounded by late training at test resolution, i.e. 32 px samples × updates in the final phase, not by total steps or total epochs. Every way of shrinking the 32 px phase costs the same ~0.05-0.065 pp per 1% of time: the trim (E089), the equal-step 28 px substitution (E090), and the whole-epoch shift (E025). Adding updates inside the 32 px phase helps (E084/E085/E095). This competes with H10's placement-independence and with H2's view that time is the only thing that differs between phases. Two candidate mechanisms: (a) the net must re-adapt to the test-resolution input statistics after each resolution switch (stem output, BN statistics, the whitening bias); (b) full-resolution samples carry fine-detail information that the downsampled phases cannot supply.

Resolution-statistics adaptation. The antialiased downsample changes patch statistics, so each resolution switch shifts the stem-output distribution. The 64x-LR whitening bias and the BN affine parameters absorb that shift. Freezing the bias before the later switches removes this adaptation. Evidence: E093 (freezing at 0.2 epoch cost -0.44 pp off-seed and -0.5 pp scored, the largest clearly real recent effect). The current freeze sits at ~41% of samples, inside the 24 px phase, before the 28 and 32 px switches.

On the E090 config, move the whitening-bias freeze from ~41% of samples to ~70% (after the 28 px switch, inside the 32 px phase). As a second arm, never freeze it. Use the existing grad / no-grad graph variants, warmed up in build for every shape that needs them. Log the bias vector norm and its change at each resolution switch. Pre-registered time cost: +0.3-0.8% (the stem dgrad comes back). Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 against E090 on the same seeds, plus two distinct scored samples. Prediction (adaptation): the best arm gains >= +0.1 pp off-seed, i.e. >0.065 pp per 1% of time, and the bias changes visibly (>=10% of its norm) at the 28 and 32 px switches when it is still trainable. If both arms are within ±0.05 pp, the freeze point is closed, and E093's loss was early-phase fragility rather than switch adaptation.
Placement of updates: added steps at low resolution buy little or nothing, while added steps at 32 px buy ~0.1-0.18 pp (E084/E095). This is the direct rival of H10.1's placement-independence.

This is the same run as H10.1.1 (E090 config with bs 1024 also at 16/24 px, ~+50 low-res steps, +1.5-2.5% time) with the opposite prediction: an off-seed seeds 3-26 gain of <= +0.03 pp, less than half the per-step value of E084's 32 px steps (+0.11 pp per ~65 steps). If the gain is >= +0.08 pp, placement-independence holds and NL1.2 is refuted.

The bs-1024 32 px gain is a Muon path-length effect, not an update-count effect. Muon's orthogonalized update has a size set by the lr (and the shape scale), not by the gradient. At a fixed sample-indexed lr, 1.5x more steps at 32 px means ~1.5x more total filter movement (relative to ||w||, since the filters are renormed). If so, a larger Muon lr in the 32 px phase alone should reproduce the gain at zero time cost. The SGD-era adaptive-batch literature increases the batch late (search), so a late small-batch gain fits a Muon-specific mechanism better than a generic noise one.

On E086 code (bs 1536 throughout, the control config for E084), raise the conv-filter Muon lr by 1.25x (0.24 -> 0.30 peak, same schedule shape and floor) in the 32 px phase only. The head stays at 0.5x and scales along, as a phase-keyed 0-d tensor, so nothing recompiles. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 against E086 on the same seeds, plus two distinct scored samples. Prediction (path length): off-seed >= E086 +0.08 pp (at least 2/3 of E084's +0.11) at equal time (±0.5%). If the gain is <= +0.03 pp, update count rather than movement is the mechanism, and per-phase batch size (H2.11) remains the only route. If it holds, port it to the E090 config, where it would add accuracy at zero time.

Extend the one replicated accuracy lever. On the E090 config (or E095 if E090 is replaced), run the 28 and 32 px phases at bs 768 instead of bs 1024, keeping bs 1536 at 16/24 px. Index by samples; scale the SGD groups by the kilostep rule; keep Muon lr/momentum unchanged; pin the final-EMA window to the last 8 steps as in E095; warm up the static bs-768 shapes in build. Pre-registered time: +3-4.5% (~+80-90 steps at ~1.7 ms). Prediction: off-seed seeds 3-26 gain >= +0.25 pp over the same base, and two distinct scored samples with mean >= base +0.2 pp, i.e. above the 0.065 pp per 1% bar. A gain of <= +0.12 pp means returns are diminishing below bs 1024, and the per-phase batch line is exhausted.

In build, set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark_limit=0 so cuDNN v8 tries every available conv algorithm for each static train shape (16/24/28/32 px, bs 1536/1024) and the eval path, instead of the default 10. Change nothing else, and check that build stays under 600 s. Log per-phase epoch times and per-(layer, shape) conv kernel names against the E090 defaults, which also feeds H4.5.1. Prediction: at least one 24/28/32 px shape picks a different kernel, and mean total time falls by >=0.8% over two scored runs. Accuracy is math-equivalent within noise (distinct pool within 0.1 pp of the E090 family). If the kernel names are identical to the default picks, or time changes by <0.3%, the lever is closed.

Depth cuts as a time lever. Width cuts failed because of tile quantization (E080: 352/320 recovered only 33-60% of the FLOP-proportional time). Removing a whole conv per group (airbench94 uses 2 convs per group where this net's airbench96 lineage uses 3) removes entire cuDNN kernels and ~23 elementwise kernels per block, so the saving should be close to proportional. Capacity is valuable on CIFAR-100 (E017, E050), so the cut must save enough to fund >= +0.5 epoch at 32 px plus the lost capacity. Prior is low.

Untimed first. Profile per-step time and NVML energy at 32 px, bs 1024, for the E090 net with (a) group-1 conv3 removed (31x31 map) and (b) group-3 conv3 removed. Prediction: at least one variant cuts total run time by >=6% when projected over the E090 schedule. Score only that variant, with the 32 px phase lengthened to spend half the saving: an expected net time of ~-3%, with off-seed seeds 3-26 within 0.05 pp of E090. If neither variant saves >=6%, close depth cuts without a scored run.

The judge is a 300 W A100 PCIe; local runs are on a 400 W SXM4. Untimed analysis of existing NVML logs (E045 and later), with no power-limit changes: project each candidate's judge time as the sum over phases of max(phase energy / 300 W, phase GPU-busy time). Prediction: the E090-vs-E095 time gap widens by >=1.1x on the projected PCIe times, because the 32 px work that E090 swaps for 28 px is energy-bound. Per-step levers (bs 1024 at 32 px) cost relatively more there. Use the projection only to break ties between configs whose measured local times are within 3%.

Extended off-seed instrument and tip decision. Run the unchanged E090 config and the E095 config through the benchmark's trial code on seeds 3-26 (24 seeds), one fresh process each, logging weight checksums. Prediction: per-seed sd is 0.22-0.38 pp, so the SE of a 24-seed mean is ~0.05-0.08 pp. E090's 24-seed mean is <=0.7530 (consistent with ~0.7524), and E095's is >=0.7540. If both hold, E095 (4.70 s) is the only robustly feasible config, and E090 must gain >=+0.1 pp (NL1.1.1, NH10P.1, H6.5.4, NBL-neutral) before it can be called banked. All later off-seed A/Bs use seeds 3-26 against these baselines.
